The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

The test only uses one data provider (`data_plus`) out of many. Let me check the CUT's `minus` signature, then write a clean version.Now I'll write the refactored test. Key issues: 11 of 12 data providers are unused, ~20 imports are unused, and the parameter names obscure the minus semantics (the test calls `minus` on the *end* date to get back the *start* date).Compiles cleanly (`COMPILE_OK`). The refactored test removes 11 unused data providers and ~30 unused imports, renames the provider to `data_minus` with a doc comment explaining the start/amount/unit/end columns, and renames the parameters so the inverse-of-plus `minus` semantics are clear — all while calling `minus` with the same arguments and asserting the same outcomes as the original.
